V01: A dispersed academic campus organized around a freestanding classroom block and a connected pair of shared-use volumes. Core academics and special education form a vertically layered teaching precinct, while a separate arts, media center, and support block connects directly to the recreation and dining volume. The composition establishes two distinct building clusters.
V02: A linear three-part composition with the recreation and arts volume acting as the connecting hinge between two vertically organized learning blocks. One block combines core academics, an upper-level media center, and administration, while the other concentrates special education and support functions. The sequence forms a linked chain without a direct connection between its academic ends.
V03: A dispersed three-pavilion campus with each mass operating as an independent architectural element. A vertically organized core academic and special education block stands apart from a recreation and dining pavilion, while a third block combines ground-level arts and administration with an elevated media center. The arrangement is defined by separation rather than internal building links.
V04: Three detached programmatic volumes organized by distinct institutional roles. A consolidated academic building layers classrooms, special education, the media center, and support functions vertically. A separate recreation and dining pavilion includes administration, while art and music occupy an independent studio volume. The overall composition emphasizes three autonomous masses without direct connecting links.
V05: A paired academic and student-support cluster set apart from an independent recreation and arts pavilion. The core classroom block connects directly to a vertically layered special education, administration, and media center block, forming the primary academic grouping. The detached third volume places creative learning above recreation and dining, establishing a separate stacked activity element.
V06: A detached three-volume organization separating academic learning, recreation, and shared institutional resources. Core academics and special education occupy one consolidated teaching block, with health and maintenance functions at its base. A separate recreation and dining pavilion stands independently, as does an arts and administration block with the media center elevated above its ground-level functions.
V07: A fully interconnected triangular campus organized around a consolidated learning block and two complementary shared-use volumes. Core academics, special education, arts, and the media center are layered within a single teaching mass. A compact administrative and support block and a recreation and dining volume complete the triangle, with direct links joining all three elements.
V08: A tripartite detached campus with independent academic, specialized learning, and recreation volumes. The main academic building combines classrooms with administration at its base and the media center at its upper level. A second three-story block groups special education with arts and support functions, while recreation and dining occupy a separate pavilion without direct connections to either learning block.
V09: A fully connected three-mass composition forming a triangular network between complementary educational precincts. A core academic block combines classrooms with an upper-level media center and ground-level administration. A parallel special education and arts block provides another vertically organized learning environment, while recreation and dining form the third volume, directly linking the two educational elements.
V10: A linear sequence of three connected programmatic volumes, with an arts, media center, and support block serving as the intermediate connector. Core academics and special education form one vertically layered end, while recreation and dining occupy the opposite end. The central shared-resource element links both termini without a direct connection between them.
V11: A fully interconnected triangular arrangement of three specialized volumes. The core academic block, a special education and student-support block, and a recreation and arts block each maintain a distinct programmatic identity. The media center crowns the student-support volume, while art and music occupy the upper level of the recreation volume. Direct links complete the three-sided network.
V12: A linear three-part school organized around a central recreation and dining connector. One end contains a compact administration and media center block, with the media center raised above administrative functions. The opposite end consolidates core academics, special education, arts, and support programs into a layered teaching mass. The middle volume directly links the two ends.
V13: A branching three-mass composition with recreation and dining acting as the central connector between two distinct learning blocks. One branch organizes special education, administration, and an elevated media center, while the other combines core academics with upper-level arts and ground-level maintenance. The two learning branches remain unlinked to each other, producing a hinged configuration.
V14: A fully interconnected triangular school composed of three complementary vertical program blocks. Core academics, administration, and the media center form one learning volume, while special education is stacked over a recreation and dining base in another. A third compact block houses arts, health, and maintenance functions. Direct connections between every pair create a closed three-part network.
V15: A two-part connected cluster accompanied by a freestanding core academic building. The connected pair joins a vertically layered special education, administration, and media center block to a recreation volume crowned by art and music. The separate classroom block retains its own three-story academic identity, establishing a primary linked activity cluster alongside an independent teaching mass.
V16: A detached main teaching block paired with a connected shared-resource and recreation cluster. Core academics and special education are vertically consolidated with administration at the base, forming an independent educational mass. The second cluster joins a layered arts and media center block to the recreation and dining volume, establishing a two-part support and activity grouping apart from classrooms.
V17: A linear three-volume arrangement with recreation and dining forming the intermediate link between two separate learning blocks. Core academics rise toward an upper-level media center above ground-level administration at one end. At the other, special education occupies a three-story block alongside arts and support functions. The middle pavilion connects both ends without a direct academic-to-academic link.
V18: A linked three-part sequence organized around a central recreation and dining volume. At one end, a compact institutional block stacks the media center above administration, medical, and maintenance functions. At the other, a consolidated teaching block contains core academics, special education, and ground-level arts. The central activity volume connects the two otherwise separate blocks.
V19: A fully connected triangular composition organized around three differentiated program zones. One combines special education and administration with a recreation and dining base; another consolidates core academics with ground-level arts; and the third concentrates the media center above medical and maintenance functions. Direct links between all three establish an interconnected network of learning, activity, and shared resources.
V20: A paired academic and recreation cluster accompanied by a detached student-support building. The core academic block places the media center at its upper level and connects directly to a recreation volume with art and music elevated above it. A separate two-story special education block combines medical and administrative functions, remaining physically independent of the connected academic and activity pair.
V21: A linear three-part school with a special education and support block operating as the connecting hinge. A consolidated academic and arts volume stacks classrooms, creative spaces, and an upper-level media center at one end. Recreation and dining occupy the other end, connected through the intermediate special education, administration, and medical block rather than directly to the academic volume.
V22: A branching configuration centered on a consolidated academic and creative-learning building. Core academics, special education, and ground-level arts form the primary vertical teaching mass. Two distinct connected branches extend from it: an administrative, medical, and maintenance block, and a recreation volume supporting an elevated media center. The two branches remain disconnected from each other.
V23: A branched three-mass composition with the core academic building acting as the central connector. Its three-story classroom structure and ground-level support functions link directly to a dedicated recreation and dining pavilion and to a specialized learning block. The latter combines special education, arts, administration, and an elevated media center, while the two attached branches remain mutually unconnected.
V24: A linear three-part arrangement with a recreation and arts volume as the central hinge. The main classroom block connects to one side, while a special education, administration, and media center block connects to the other. Creative learning is elevated above the recreation base, and the two academic blocks remain separate except through their shared intermediate volume.
V25: A detached main academic building accompanied by a linked special education and activity cluster. Core classrooms occupy a vertically organized block with ground-level administration and an upper-level media center. Separately, the special education and arts block connects directly to the recreation, dining, and medical volume. The composition establishes an independent primary academic element beside a connected secondary grouping.
V26: A fully interconnected triangular arrangement with a compact shared-resource block mediating between teaching and activity volumes. The academic mass consolidates core classrooms, special education, and arts, while the resource mass places the media center above ground-level administration, medical, and maintenance functions. Recreation and dining complete the triangle, with each volume directly linked to the other two.
V27: A linear three-part configuration with the recreation and dining volume forming the central connector. A vertically consolidated core academic and special education block anchors one end, while an arts and institutional support block with an elevated media center anchors the other. Both terminal blocks connect to the middle activity volume but have no direct link to one another.
V28: A two-volume academic and shared-resource cluster set apart from an independent recreation and administration pavilion. The main teaching block vertically combines core academics, special education, and arts. It connects directly to a support volume crowned by the media center, with medical and maintenance functions below. The recreation volume remains detached, carrying administration alongside its ground-level activity programs.
V29: A dispersed three-pavilion composition with no direct links between its constituent masses. One vertically layered teaching volume combines core academics, special education, and medical functions. A second pavilion contains recreation and dining, while a third concentrates arts, administration, and maintenance beneath an elevated media center. The organization maintains three separate programmatic identities across the site.
V30: A detached consolidated teaching block and a connected shared-resource and activity pair. The teaching volume vertically integrates core academics and special education with ground-level arts, medical, and maintenance functions. Separately, a compact administration and media center block connects to recreation and dining, establishing a two-mass institutional cluster independent of the principal classroom building.
V31: A detached core learning block accompanied by a connected arts, support, and recreation cluster. Core academics and special education are vertically consolidated beneath an upper-level media center in one independent mass. A separate arts and support block connects directly to the recreation and dining volume, creating a linked activity grouping with no direct building connection to the academic mass.
V32: A linear three-volume school organized around an intermediate arts and shared-resource block. The core academic and special education mass forms one end of the sequence, while recreation and dining form the other. Between them, creative learning, administration, medical functions, and an upper-level media center occupy the connecting volume, linking the two termini without a direct connection.
V33: A fully interconnected triangular composition of academic, shared-activity, and creative-support volumes. The primary academic mass combines core classrooms and special education across three levels, with the media center at the top. A recreation and dining volume incorporates administration, while a separate ground-level arts, medical, and maintenance block completes the network. All three masses are directly linked.
V34: A central recreation and administration volume connected to the main teaching block, with a detached arts and media center pavilion. Core academics and special education occupy a vertically consolidated classroom mass, linked directly to recreation, dining, medical, and administrative functions. The independent creative-learning pavilion places the media center above art and music, forming a separate third element.
V35: A fully interconnected triangular arrangement combining three distinctly layered program volumes. The main teaching mass consolidates core academics and special education, while a compact administrative and health block places the media center above its ground-level functions. The recreation and dining volume supports an upper-level arts component. Direct connections among all three establish a closed spatial network.
